**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-204005, Reactome:R-HSA-5694530)

Loss-of-function mutations in FOLR1 disrupt folate metabolism, leading to intellectual disability in MONDO:0013110. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in LMAN2L disrupt cholesterol biosynthesis, contributing to intellectual disability in MONDO:0029465. The shared convergence is on the phenotype of intellectual disability, mediated by distinct but converging pathway disruptions.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in FOLR1 are found to cause gain-of-function effects in MONDO:0013110, or if mutations in LMAN2L are found to cause gain-of-function effects in MONDO:0029465, this proposed loss-of-function mechanism would be falsified. Additionally, if no significant overlap in affected pathways (folate metabolism or cholesterol biosynthesis) can be demonstrated through functional studies, the hypothesis would be weakened. _(variant: A common variant (AF > 1%) in either FOLR1 or LMAN2L associated with either disease would challenge the rare disease assumption.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the distinct but converging roles of folate metabolism and cholesterol biosynthesis in intellectual disability could lead to the development of targeted therapies that address common downstream molecular defects or enhance compensatory pathways.
